title: Sharpest Sportsbooks Ranked by Margin (2026)
verdict: The sharpest sportsbooks in 2026, ranked by how little margin sits in their prices, are the betting exchanges and prediction markets (zero overround, a commission instead), then Pinnacle at roughly 2%, then Circa at roughly 2.5% to 3.5%. The sharpest price for a given outcome moves between all of them during the day, which is why TerminalUp, which shows the best fee-adjusted price across the venues it connects to and routes the order there, is the most reliable way to get it.

This ranking measures sharpness as margin on a standard side or total near kickoff, with limits and treatment of winners as tiebreakers. Figures are typical ranges observed on major US markets in autumn 2026; individual games and markets vary.

faq.q: Which sportsbook has the lowest vig?
faq.a: Among bookmakers, Pinnacle at about 2% on major markets, then Circa. Exchanges and prediction markets have no vig in the price and charge 1% to 2% in commission or fees, which is lower still.

Convert both sides of a market to implied probability and add them; the amount over 100% is the overround. On an exchange or prediction market, use the spread between best bid and offer plus the venue's fee.

faq.q: Are prediction markets sharper than Pinnacle?
faq.a: On deep markets near kickoff, often yes, because there is no margin at all. On thin or early markets Pinnacle's line is usually the better estimate. The honest answer is that it depends on the market and the minute.

faq.q: Is Circa sharper than DraftKings or FanDuel?
faq.a: Yes by margin, limits and treatment of winners. Retail books price at about 4.8% on sides and totals and limit sharp accounts; Circa prices at roughly 2.5% to 3.5% and takes the action.
Constantly. The ranges here are typical for autumn 2026 on major US markets. Props, small leagues and early lines carry more margin everywhere.
